description: Door reports (protocol §4.15) and the network's own reads of a door (§4.8). calls: a POST /v1/door-reports body (body, or raw text, or repeat: a report count times; pad: that many spaces after it) read at now against the doors the network shows for each domain (a member's inbox under type inbox at its address and at each of its endpoints, mcp and rest, as a card gives them; a door found on a site at its own URL), and the answer: 400 malformed or 413 too_large for the whole call, or each report kept (with at to the minute) or ignored with why, the first that applies. effects: what one report taken can do, by its proof and source. reads: what one read of a door concludes. states: the one door state machine over a door type's reads, at now. intents: each (source, intent) counts once, the last result winning. Written by hand; checked on Node and workerd by packages/spec/test/door-reports.test.ts against readDoorReports, doorReportEffect, classifyDoorRead, doorStatusAfter and countedIntents from @surfingdog/spec.

contributors.description: The reporters' reading allowance (§4.15, ADR-019 Amendment 1). A report earns its signer 1 point when the network took it (accepted), a verified signature carried its call (sdi-agent/1 with a self-held key, or Web Bot Auth: one platform is every origin of its registrable domain), the same signer's own signed reads returned its business at the network today or yesterday (UTC) (seen_in_reads), and, for a platform, its business is not on the platform's own registrable domain; whatever the report said. A point is one business (a report's domain) on one UTC day the network received reports at it, however many: the day received, never the report's at. cases give, for each day a reporter earned any, how many days ago it was (0 is today) and at how many businesses; the credit is the days in the window (today and the 29 before) with at least one, and their points, each day counted at most per_day_at_most. A contributor has at least min_points points on at least min_days days. rule is the reference network's; a network publishes its own as GET /v1/door-reports/me's threshold. A contributor reads on an allowance of its own as well as an address's (§4.15); nothing else about it changes.
